correctness.rationale: Reconstructed P(z)=zᵀAz with b_ij=2A_ij and E=2||A||_F²−Σ|A_ii|², and verified spectral/Takagi op-norm identity and convexity reduction to symmetric real orthogonal / complex unitary matrices. Odd real trace |tr U|≥1 forces δ≥1/n, attained by constant-diagonal Fourier projection; even dimensions have transposition blocks. In complex n=3 the cofactor/row-orthogonality inequality (3−δ)/2≤√(3δ)+δ forces δ≥1/3 and Householder attains it. Symmetric zero-diagonal 5-point Fourier unitary with cosθ=−1/4 and 2×2 sums attain δ=0 in every other n≥2. n=1 agrees with both fields. These arguments cover all n analytically; no reliance on numerical sampling.
residual_risks: Claims outside exact stated normalization, field, and domain have not been proved.
